thread:
ava: Heads-up — ran a small canary this morning for p95-driven token budgets. Saw a spike on /chat/route-B when the KV hit rate dropped.

raj: Can you paste the top-line numbers? p95 before/after? :eyes:

ava: Before change (baseline): p95=188ms, p99=420ms. Canary (dynamic token target by tier): p95=195ms, p99=680ms. CPU on host increased ~8%. KV hit rate dropped from 92% -> 61% for that route.

maya: Oof, big p99 regression. Do we know why KV hit dropped? cache churn or different prefixes?

ava: Perf-bot profile attached (summary below). Looks like batch formation shifted — more short requests joined same minibatch, causing more KV evictions because active KV entries exceeded our local LRU window.

perf-bot: automated-profile: session=canary-6054321; top-samples: kernel_dispatch (43%), kv_lookup (21%), microbatch_merge (15%), kv_eviction (9%). Link: https://redwood.internal/perf/6054321 :robot_face:

raj: That suggests batching heuristics changed distribution. Which policy did canary flip?

ava: We enabled "aggressive-join" for latency SLOs: lowers min-wait and raises join-threshold for tier=gold routes. Also enabled lightweight kernel_prefetch for fp16 kernels.

tom: Kernel prefetch should help tail if compute-bound, but if kv_lookup moved up that's memory/cache problem. Did we change eviction thresholds?

ava: No direct eviction change. But aggregate token budgets per-route increased for gold, so minibatch sizes grew during bursts. More unique prefixes per batch -> larger KV working set per GPU.

maya: So dynamic token budget tradeoff: fewer queues waiting (helping p50) but increases KV footprint and some p95/p99 regressions. We need a guard for KV working set.

raj: Ideas: 1) damp aggressive-join when local-kv-hit < X. 2) add cohorting so requests with same recent prefix are preferred to batch. 3) fallback to conservative token cap when kernel_prefetch spikes memory pressure.

ava: Tried (1) locally: metric `local_kv_hit` threshold 0.75. With damping p95 improved to 190ms and p99 back to ~430ms. Throughput dropped slightly.

perf-bot: ab_test: canary-6054321 -> damp-kv-guard applied; results: p95 change -2.6%, p99 change -35%.

tom: Nice. Cohorting (2) sounds promising but needs cheap locality estimation. Maybe use most-recent-token-hash mod N as a fast binning to bias batcher?

maya: Agree. Also suggest we instrument `kv_active_set_size` per GPU in the batcher and surface as alert if >70% of eviction window.

raj: For kernel selection side: when we see larger minibatches with diverse seq-lens, kernel_prefetch may pick wide-kernel which increases memory. Could dynamically pick narrow kernel with more microbatches if kv pressure high.

ava: Good point. Proposed rule: if kv_active_set > 0.7 * eviction_cap -> prefer safe_kernel_mode and reduce token_budget by 20% for that route tier for next 30s. Implemented as simple feedback loop in runtime.

maya: We should add a short experiment: 1) baseline, 2) aggressive-join, 3) aggressive-join + kv-damp, 4) aggressive-join + kv-damp + cohorting. Run each for 2 hours during low traffic.

tom: Also capture kernel-switch counts, kv_eviction/sec, p95/p99, and tail GPU mem usage. Put dashboards in the canary board.

ava: I'll push a patch with kv-damp + telemetry and the `safe_kernel_mode` gate. PR in about an hour: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7482 :thumbsup:

raj: Thanks. One more ask — add a debug flag to log batch composition (prefix fingerprint + seq_len) at 1/1000 samples to help cohorting heuristics later.

ava: Will do.

perf-bot: deploy-event: canary-6054321-kv-damp rolled to 5% of gold traffic at 6054321120.

maya: Great. Keep eyes on p99 for route-B and kv_hit. If regression returns, we rollback. :thinking:

ava: Noted. I'll post quick follow-ups in this thread after the 30m and 2h marks.

raj: Thanks all.
